statement.p: Sketch, on a sheet of work paper, an accurate graph of f, and use it to find each of
Then find the value of the integral:

p.em: (Note that you can do this in two different ways!)

static.solution:
x=4, we are given that f(4)=0. Moving to the left on the interval 2 \lt x \lt 4, we have f'(x) = -1, and we can find f(2) by knowing that the change in f(x) over this interval is equal to the area under f'(x) between x=2 and x=4. Thus f(4) - f(2) = (-1)(2), so that f(2) = f(4) - (2)(-1) = 2. Similarly, continuing back to x=0, f(0) = f(2) - (1)(1) - (1)(-1) = 2
Moving to the right from x=4, we know that f'(x) = 1 on 4 \lt x \lt 5. So, as before, f(5) = f(4) + (1)(1) = 1. Similarly, continuing to x=7, f(7) = f(5) + (1)(-3) + (1)(1) = -1.
Then, the value of the integral \int_0^7 f'(x)\,dx is given by the sum \int_0^7 f'(x)\,dx = (-1)(1) + (1)(1) + (-1)(2) + (1)(1) + (-3)(1) + (1)(1) = -3.
Alternatively, knowing f(7)=-1 and f(0)=2 and using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, we have \int_0^7 f'(x)\,dx=f(7)-f(0) = (-1) - (2) = -3.
